name: Savitri Jindal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2018); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: O.P. Jindal Group, whose interests include steel, power, cement and infrastructure, is chaired by Savitri Jindal, widow of founder Om Prakash Jindal.
Upon O.P. Jindal's death in 2005 in a helicopter crash, the group's companies were divided among his four sons, who now run them independently.
The biggest assets of  the group are overseen by her Mumbai-based son Sajjan Jindal, who oversees JSW Steel, JSW Cement and JSW Paints, among much else.
In 2024, Sajjan Jindal set up an EV joint venture with MG Motor, which has since sold 100,000 EVS. In 2025, he took JSW Cement public
Jindal's younger, Delhi-based son, Naveen, manages Jindal Steel & Power. In March 2024, he quit the Congress party and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party.
forbes_facts: O.P. Jindal got his start making buckets in 1952, then went on to found a pipe unit named Jindal India in 1964.
The family's cement arm JSW Cement was listed in August 2025 at a small premium to its issue price.

name: Jorge Paulo Lemann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Jorge Paulo Lemann is a co-founder and partner in private equity firm 3G Capital, best known for its investments in Anheuser-Busch InBev and Restaurant Brands International, parent of Burger King and Canadian coffee chain Tim Hortons.
Lemann's billionaire partners in 3G include fellow Brazilians Carlos Sicupira, Marcel Herrmann Telles and Alex Behring.
Jorge Paulo Lemann started in investment banking and later became a controlling shareholder of Anheuser-Busch InBev, the world's largest brewer.
3G sold its stake in U.S. condiment maker Kraft-Heinz in 2024 after 11 years.
In 2021, 3G acquired 75% of Dutch window shade company Hunter Douglas in a $7 billion transaction, and in 2025 paid almost $10 billion for U.S sneaker brand Skechers.

name: Leon Black
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Leon Black is the cofounder of private equity behemoth Apollo Global Management, which manages $1 trillion in assets.
Black stepped down as Apollo's CEO and chairman in 2021 after a board investigation found that he paid $158 million in fees to Jeffrey Epstein. A further investigation upped the sum to $170 million.
Black spent much of his early career at investment bank Drexel Burnham Lambert, where he eventually headed the mergers and acquisitions group.
After Drexel filed for bankruptcy in 1990, Black founded Apollo with colleagues Joshua Harris and Marc Rowan, both of whom are billionaires.
Apollo went public in 2011; Black still owns roughly 7% of the company's shares.
forbes_facts: An avid art collector, Black spent $120 million in 2012 for one of four versions of Edvard Munch's painting "The Scream."
Black and his wife, Debra, a melanoma survivor, have given millions of dollars to the Melanoma Research Alliance.

name: Dmitry Bukhman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2022-2023)
forbes_bio: Dmitry Bukhman and his brother Igor own online gaming upstart Playrix.
The company is best known for free mobile-app games such as Homescapes and Fishdom.
Born and raised in northern Russia, the brothers started selling games online while Dmitry was still in high school.
Playrix now does more than $2.7 billion in estimated annual revenue.
In 2018, the Bukhman brothers acquired a stake in video and social network games developer Nexters Global.

name: Bruce Kovner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Bruce Kovner is chairman of CAM Capital, founded in 2012, which manages his personal investment and business portfolios.
Kovner is the founder and former chairman of Caxton Associates, a global macro hedge fund.
He retired from the hedge fund in 2011 after running it for three decades.
A longtime backer of conservative think tank American Enterprise Institute, Kovner also supports the Met Opera, Lincoln Center and the Juilliard School.
forbes_facts: Kovner once worked as a cab driver in New York City.
Kovner took classes at the Juilliard School, where he chaired the board for more than two decades.

name: Samuel I. Jr. And Donald E. Newhouse
Maria Del Pino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Maria del Pino's fortune stems from her 9% stake in Spanish infrastructure giant Ferrovial SE, part of which she inherited from her late father.
Her father founded Ferrovial in 1952; it manages airports and highways around the world including London's Heathrow Airport.
She has been a member of the board of Ferrovial, which trades on the Euronext Amsterdam and Madrid stock exchanges.
She is also the chairman of the family's charitable foundation, Fundación Del Pino.
Her brother Rafael del Pino is the chairman of Ferrovial and its largest individual shareholder.
